docs.purpose: Lets an admin send one real test push notification to a specific device or user to verify the notification pipeline works end to end, without it counting against that user's daily notification limit or appearing in the normal send history.
docs.data_story: It reads 1 table — `device_tokens` and writes nothing. Its response is an explicit pick-by-name projection of 6 fields, so a column added to a table upstream does not leak into the client by accident. It is called from 1 place: `admin_notifications`.
docs.under_126: Becomes a **CONTRACT descriptor** of archetype `COMMAND`. It declares the JOB it triggers (`job_ref`), its concurrency posture and the audit row it must write. Its `consumers[]` becomes the edge list of the fan-out graph — the join nothing in this estate holds today.

notes: Deliberately writes NO DB rows (no notification_dispatches ledger row, no notifications queue row) so a test send does not consume the user's once-per-day dedup slot. Sends the real push by dynamically importing scripts/lib/push-dispatch.js (sendPushChunk), the same transport the production dispatcher uses. Requires authMethod === 'session' (403 for admin_key/dev_bypass shared identities). Mutating externally but writes no admin audit row. | MEASURED 2026-09-15: Census checklist: the one named table (device_tokens) VERIFIED. Census MISSED `profiles` (verifyAdminAuth, src/lib/auth/verify-admin.ts:117-120). FINDINGS: (1) DEFECT — malformed JSON returns 502 SEND_FAILED, not 400 (see input_validation above; request.json() at :60 is unguarded). (2) NO AUDIT ROW for a real side effect that reaches a user's device: only a PostHog event (:110-114), no admin_audit_log, and by design no notification_dispatches row (:10-12) — so an operator-sent push is invisible in the DB ledger. (3) An explicit push_token in the body bypasses the device_tokens lookup entirely (:69-70), so an admin can push to ANY Expo token, including one not belonging to any user of this system — there is no ownership check on the supplied token. (4) The error message returned on 502 is the raw Expo/transport error truncated to 300 chars (:133); the comment at :130-131 asserts it contains no secrets — a claim, not evidence, though the token is indeed in the request rather than the error. (5) The delegate is loaded by a deep relative dynamic import '../../../../../../scripts/lib/push-dispatch.js' (:88-90) — fragile to any route relocation and outside the src/ tree, so it escapes the src/-scoped ESLint rules named in CLAUDE.md §5. (6) The payload hard-codes notification_type LIFECYCLE_PHASE_CHANGED and _test_send:true (:99-103); the receiving client's handling of _test_send was not researched (out of scope for this route file). | Caching: none observed — no Cache-Control, no dynamic/revalidate, no in-process memo in route.ts:1-137 | Other guards / classification: CSRF Origin allowlist DOES apply (POST is in MUTATING_METHODS, src/lib/auth/verify-admin.ts:45, checked at :70-78, default-deny at :336). MFA gate inert unless ADMIN_MFA_ENFORCED=true (src/lib/auth/verify-admin.ts:143). No replay/nonce protection — the same body can be POSTed repeatedly. | Locking tests: src/tests/admin-notifications.infra.test.ts.
